project_scope.note: Built as the companion half of the elm-vs-hackberry comparison.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start at the leaf base and venation: local Celtis commonly has three strong primary veins arising from near the base.
family_diagnostics.leaves: Alternate simple leaves, often asymmetric; margins entire or toothed depending on species.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Thinly fleshy drupe with hard stone.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Three basal veins + fleshy drupe is the fastest local Celtis combination.

look_here_first_sequence.cue: At a leaf base, trace the three strong basal or near-basal veins common in Celtis; do not diagnose from venation alone.
Examine an individual flower: small, inconspicuous flowers can show exposed anthers; distinguish them from showy petals.
Confirm a separate fleshy drupe with one hard stone; distinguish from elm/Planera dry fruits and Morus multiple fruits.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Hackberries become easy once you stop asking 'elm or hackberry?' and trace the veins from the petiole.

steps.title: 1 · Trace the three basal veins
steps.look_for: Three strong veins leaving the base or near-base of the leaf.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the best quick separation from Ulmus.

steps.title: 2 · Confirm with the drupe
steps.look_for: A small fleshy drupe with a hard stone.

steps.title: 3 · Read the whole tree
steps.look_for: Woody Celtis architecture with alternate leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects the diagnostic leaf/fruit to whole-plant gestalt.

steps.title: 4 · See the netleaf form
steps.look_for: Prominent netted venation layered onto the basal-vein Celtis plan.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows genus-level variation without losing the family cues.

comparisons.title: Cannabaceae vs Ulmaceae
comparisons.rule: Celtis = strong basal 3-vein pattern + fleshy drupe. Ulmus = many pinnate side veins into serrations + dry samara.

comparisons.title: Bark is secondary
comparisons.rule: Hackberry bark can be corky/warty, but leaf venation and fruit are safer first characters.

comparisons.title: Cannabaceae vs Moraceae
comparisons.rule: Celtis bears individual drupes; Morus makes a multiple fruit from a flower cluster. Basal leaf veins overlap.

comparisons.title: Cannabaceae vs Rhamnaceae
comparisons.rule: Basal veins alone overlap. Compare flower anatomy, stipules/thorns and mature fruit before deciding.

visual_lesson.caveat: Modern classification places Celtis in Cannabaceae, not Ulmaceae.
